commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Nathan's UBR 3/2 Rogue attack trigger exiles one top card from every library and permits one PAID spell cast during resolution. Multiplier attacks and pre-resolution combat mana, rather than damage-triggered secondary theft, maximize his unique four-library heist.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 4 Optimized: low-cost heist commander with premier resources, repeated attacks and interaction; opponent-dependent hits and payment windows are not a deterministic fast cEDH kill.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Preserve direct Nathan attack triggers, a high density of stolen/unowned spell payoffs, free/cheap response protection and supporting independent theft. Avoid Oracle/Breach generic Grixis win shells and additive high-cost passive theft that fails to fund attack triggers.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Every one of the approved 99 noncommander physical slots re-challenged against the October 15 exact TXT and October 19 exhaustive 100-card M6 deck-depth artifact. Core trigger multiplication, exile payoffs, cheap counterspells, broad removal and Rogue/stealing subtheme preserved. The re-challenge finds six damage- or upkeep-delayed independent theft slots, one symmetrical opponent-payoff, a Dauthi/Tinybones tension, one damage-only equipment and own-turn pitch counter misaligned with Nathan's main attack window.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: 34 lands preserved, including six basic copies, all nine typed-dual-compatible fetches, three premium duals/shocks and Fire Nation Palace. RRR/BBB costs and any-color spend restriction remain distinct. Three fast-mana replacements reduce average nonland mana demand; Chrome Mox imprint card cost and Vault/Monolith untap taxes are real. Palace and attack Treasures can pay inside combat; Jeska's Will main-phase mana cannot float to that window.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Keep An Offer You Can't Refuse, Swan Song, Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship, Deadly Rollick, Deflecting Swat, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Blasphemous Act and artifact answer You Find Some Prisoners. Force of Will improves free counter coverage on Nathan's own turn relative to Force of Negation. Cutting Hostage Taker was rejected because the deck needs artifact/creature access.

low_swap_heightened_audit.off_ranked_opportunities: Outside EDHREC High Lift and the October 15 finished deck's top-candidate pool, the strongest missed commander-native cluster is combat-window resources and repeated attack priority. Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Chrome Mox, Lannery, Dolmen Gate, Seize the Day and Sakashima were challenged as a coherent multi-card portfolio with card disadvantage and over-commitment assessed.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: Selected eleven-swap coherent current package. It recasts delayed standalone theft slots as heist-mana, direct extra attacks and protection while preserving 34 lands and core Grixis exile payoffs.
Full 13-swap fast mana/wipe challenger, recorded as exact alternative TXT; accelerates ideal hands but discards a land from 34 and replaces often one-mana mass damage with life-intensive Deluge.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Revisited the original October 15 rejections of Sakashima, Spark Double, Strionic Resonator, Combat Celebrant, Seize the Day, Access Tunnel and Spider-Verse under different cuts. Sakashima now beats generic Notion Thief, Celebrant beats symmetrical Gonti and Seize beats expensive Etali; Resonator under the Hostage Taker alternative and Spider-Verse against Fire Lord Azula still lose exact-role value.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: The October 15 list already has extensive tuned stolen-card density, free Etali casts, monarchy resources, damage-trigger creature thieves and fifteen interactive ways to play through disruption; removing too much card access could make the deck a fast-mana pile with too few spells of its own.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Retain the highest-yield independent theft (Plargg and Nassari, Gríma, Black Cat, Hostage Taker, Laughing Jasper, Tasha, Vaan), actual exile-cast rewards and the full Nathan attack-core. Replace redundancy and symmetrical cards where strict combat-window benefit is proven, preserve the land count and verify active cast payment and extra-combat conditions against Scryfall with finite source-grounded tests.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After candidate reached five true swaps, audited all remaining October 15 noncommander slots again using source-list and comprehensive October 19 per-card role ledger. In particular re-tested Plargg and Nassari, Hostage Taker, Rev, Blasphemous Act, Black Cat, Web Watch, Wild-Magic Sorcerer and every land. Found eleven, not five, quality-positive replacements. Maintained core payoff/card-volume density and cheap stack answers.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: More combats only when 5-mana Razer hits players versus up to two free stolen spells each upkeep, a meaningful independent commander-failure fallback.
A potentially extra four-library heist costs two tap mana every attack and removes scarce artifact/creature interaction.
Deluge clears indestructible and scales -X but costs life and cannot preserve 2-toughness Nathan while clearing medium blockers.
Accelerates first combat by a turn in ideal hands but discards one of only 34 lands and worsens repeated UBR commander cast reliability.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Try even faster cast with zero-mana Diamond and compact three-mana universal -X board wipe; full 100 still has six basics and same 34 lands.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Discard-land costs exceed speed value under fetch-heavy UBR land count; paid-life wipe is not strictly better than one-mana Blasphemous in creature tables.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Increase nominal Nathan combat and attack-trigger frequency with two more repeat/activation engines.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Razer requires damage and cannot attack same player; Resonator taxes scarce mana in cast window and removes artifact interaction. Both are less reliable than high-value incumbents.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: Stopped after 11 selected swaps because the strongest materially larger complete packages both create a clear loss: discarded lands/paid-life sweeper displace reliable fast fixing and low-cost global removal, and the extra-combat/trigger-copy pair sacrifices removal and free stole spells for damage-dependent or resource-hungry repetition. Notion Thief, Etali and monarchy losses were already weighed; additional candidates remaining are low-synergy or worse in an exact named slot. This is a falsifiable strategic judgment, not proof of universal optimality or a simulation-derived win rate.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: 100 physical cards, 97 unique names, only 2 Islands/2 Mountains/2 Swamps repeat, exactly 34 lands, all 97 current Scryfall Commander legal UBR, all eleven adds/cuts present and none duplicated. No companion; no authorized exception needed.
